title: First studio job: coaching Billy Lee for The Coconut Grove
summary: His first studio job was recording the drums and teaching the child actor Billy Lee to mime them at Paramount.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Oh, yes I did. I left a big space out there. I was wondering what I was doing in '38 and '39 -- now I remember other things I was doing. Okay, my first studio job, okay -- my very first studio job was ... gee, it was at the Paramount. Paramount Studios called me, they had a young boy named Billy Lee, and he was in a movie with Fred MacMurray and Ozzie Nelson, his wife, her name was Harriet ...
Harriet Hilliard. That was her name. And it was starring Fred MacMurray, and the name of the movie was "The Coconut Grove" and they made it at Paramount.

And the object of this was this little boy was supposed to be a drummer and he was supposed to play. He was about 7 years old. Billy Lee. And he was supposed to close the show or something, as a drummer -- and I had to
go out and teach him to play. But I recorded and taught him what he did -- and that was my first studio job.
You say you recorded, you mean it was your drumming on the soundtrack.
